description: The chart, Figure 3, illustrates the inter-annotator agreement in relation to sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity values. The vertical axis is not labeled, but it seems to represent a measure of inter-annotator agreement or ambiguity. The chart features a nested or layered representation, with an outer ring or section displaying different shades of blue corresponding to varying levels of ambiguity standard deviation, ranging from 0.0 to 0.94, and an inner section showing different shades of blue representing maximum ambiguity values from 1 to 3. The distribution of samples across these categories is shown as percentages, with the outer ring indicating that 19.0% of samples have a standard deviation of 0.0, 47.7% have a standard deviation of 0.47, 7.0% have a standard deviation of 0.82, and 5.0% have a standard deviation of 0.94, while the inner section shows that 39.0% of samples have a maximum ambiguity of 1, 14.2% have a maximum ambiguity of 2, and 38.0% have a maximum ambiguity of 3. The bars or sections are not sorted in a specific order other than being layered, and there is no clear visual emphasis on any particular category.
